answer: Remote hardware attestation curbs Sybil attacks among agents trading basalt and dune data under a sealed cipher. Each node binds its public key inside a trusted execution environment and submits a quote signed by a chip-fused endorsement key, letting verifiers enforce one account per silicon die. Spawning fake identities thus imposes the scarce, verifiable cost of procuring separate attested chips. However, microarchitectural side-channel leaks can still expose keys and enable cloning.
